memo.verdict: Neutral; park. Kesko Oyj (KESKOB-FI) at EUR 22.74 (2026-10-06) is a 'Major Corporate Change' case laid over a slow Nordic construction recovery, and it is not compelling at this price: the company's case is sound, the shares have already paid for the part of it that can be proved, and the next per-share event is an equity issue of EUR 500-700m. The modal return is 1.7 percent a year over eighteen months (value including cash EUR 23.33 at 2028-04-06) and 5.5 percent a year over three years (EUR 26.70 at 2029-10-06), against a 20 percent bar. The gate line does not fire (management C, business quality B, predictability B, trackability B), so the park is on price and timing. Conviction medium. Progress the case only below about EUR 18 (EUR 17.7 at the record's 15.0x exit multiple; EUR 19.0 if the multiple held at 16.1x), or on evidence that moves the Finnish residential leg or the Dahl synergy to probable before the price moves.
case: - The change is internal, large and real. Management is making the Nordic technical and building trade distributor the larger half of the company through the EUR 1.2bn Dahl acquisition, funded by a bridge and EUR 500-700m of new shares. Six of the twelve internal forces are strong: a refreshed leadership team, a resourced strategy to make Building and Technical Trade the largest division (illustrative combined sales about EUR 6.8bn; Group sales of EUR 20bn and divisional sales of EUR 10bn by the early 2030s against EUR 12.5bn in 2025), standards improvement (the EUR 250m Onnela logistics centre under budget and operational from spring 2026; cost ratio 16.9 percent; capex halved in H1 2026), a geographic step into Sweden, Norway and Denmark, the acquisition step-up, and balance-sheet utilisation to 2.8x pro forma. The screen's red flags are checked: no caretaker chief executive, no presentation-only transformation, no crown-jewel sale, no debt-funded buyback; empire-building is a plausible fit because incentives weight sales and exclude transaction costs. The weaknesses on the input side: the chief executive change is 32 months old and chosen for continuity (C); guidance has been narrowed, not raised (D); the one real price move in grocery is a EUR 50m cut on 1,200 products (D); shareholder returns are flat with an issue ahead (D).

- The external force that sets the growth division's earnings is a headwind easing slowly outside Finland and not at all inside it. Direction by force: demand mixed; competition neutral after tightening; disruption a tailwind (digital adoption disproving it); political and regulatory a headwind (VAT; payment terms); supply side neutral turning to a tailwind with Dahl's scale; the company's own cycle a tailwind (comparable EBIT troughed in 2024; the Q2 2026 gain the strongest since Q1 2022); macroeconomic a headwind (Finnish variable-rate households; Norges Bank held through 2027). The 'Demand Inflection' test is not met. The professional, infrastructure and renovation leg (more than 55 percent of Building and Technical Trade sales) is growing; residential newbuild is flat on its floor with no two-year visibility in Finland; consumer demand is stable to soft.

- The change has reached the outputs unevenly along the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain. The grocery share recovery has travelled all six layers (share and margin in the statements since late 2025; DNB Carnegie's upgrade to Buy in October 2025). The Finnish technical trade recovery is at the operating metrics and statements (divisional EBIT +EUR 20.3m in Q2 2026; a beat of about 5 percent against Vara consensus) and only partly at the estimates. Dahl is at the choices-and-actions layers and in the FY2027 numbers of only two of the four named brokers.
counter_case: - Kesko is a mis-modelled Nordic distribution compounder at the bottom of its cycle. Dahl makes it the scale buyer in Nordic heating, plumbing and air-conditioning with automated warehouses and 35 percent digital sales; the division's margin went from 2.1 to 5.1 percent in the last upcycle, and the 6 to 8 percent target on about EUR 7bn of sales is EUR 420-560m of divisional EBIT against about EUR 250m today; consensus is held down by two brokers who have not consolidated Dahl and by a Finnish residential floor that cannot get lower; grocery is a bounded-downside asset; 16x is the ten-year median, a 10 percent discount to DNB Carnegie's long-run average, for a business whose quality the sell-side now rates higher than it did. On that reading the next two years bring the trajectory upgrades the 'Major Corporate Change' pattern promises and a multiple of 17.5 to 19x, and the shares reach EUR 30 or more by April 2028.

- What the record concedes: the operating leverage is real and the division's own 2017-2023 record is the precedent; a Finnish recovery from 15,000 starts toward 25,000 would fall on a right-sized cost base; the buying scale argues for more than EUR 10m of synergy; and if both arrive the fair multiple is higher than 15.0x, which is why the record names the 17.5x anchor and shows 12.0 percent a year on its own earnings. On the bull earnings (a 24-month-forward figure of about EUR 1.65 at eighteen months; divisional EBIT about EUR 1,050m by FY2029 with grocery at EUR 450m), 17.5x gives EUR 30.31 with cash, 21.1 percent a year, and 19.1x gives EUR 32.95, 28.0 percent a year; at 15.0x the same bull earnings give EUR 26.18, 9.8 percent a year. The bull case needs both legs.
triggers: - Price: progress only below about EUR 18 (EUR 17.7 at the 15.0x exit; EUR 19.0 at a held 16.1x); the 52-week low is EUR 17.10 and DNB Carnegie's bear target under a prolonged construction slump EUR 17. The pinned TSR/Valuation would not read C against the 'Modal return' until the price were near EUR 18 to 19.

- Nordic construction volume: Finnish permits above 20,000 annualised for two consecutive quarters moves the residential leg to probable and the division's FY2028 margin toward 5.5 percent; building and technical trade monthly growth converging toward the 0.6 percent competitor average takes the professional leg to possible and modal EBIT below EUR 800m. Alarm: divisional sales growth below 5 percent for two months. Invalidate: divisional comparable EBIT margin below 3.5 percent for a half-year. Rates: no Norges Bank cut by end-2027 is the alarm; Finnish starts below 15,000 in 2027 the invalidate level.

- Dahl: a first synergy disclosure above EUR 20m, or the Swedish Dahl business showing 100 basis points of margin expansion, moves the record toward the bull end; an issue above EUR 700m or below EUR 20 a share, or a Danish or Swedish EBIT miss in the first consolidated half, takes the accretion branch to possible. Invalidate: Dahl EBIT below EUR 50m in its first full year. The post-issue share count is the one unnamed link in the transmission to EPS.

- Grocery share at margin: continued sequential PTY share gains confirm; alarm at share flat for two quarters or margin below 6.5 percent; invalidate at a share loss above 50 basis points over consecutive quarters with margin below 6 percent (also the risks report's re-run trigger). S Group's next price move: alarm at grocery margin below 6.5 percent in a quarter; invalidate below 6 percent for a half-year.

- The multiple: the shares holding 16x or better through the issue and the first consolidated half would say the market accepts the distributor mix at a food-retail multiple; alarm at a multiple above 17.5x on the record's earnings without an earnings change; no invalidate level, because a valuation level is a price, not an invalidation.

- Comparable EBIT path: EUR 700m FY2026, 815m FY2027, 875m FY2028; alarm below a EUR 680m run-rate; invalidate on a guidance cut below EUR 650m. Sell-side: alarm at FY2027 consensus cut below EUR 1.25; invalidate at FY2028 cut below EUR 1.30. Cash return: alarm at payout above 100 percent; invalidate on a dividend cut. Leverage: alarm above 2.5x a year after closing; invalidate above 3.0x. Car division: alarm at divisional EBIT below Q2 2025's level in H2. Regulator: alarm at a new measure with a stated cash effect. Governance: alarm at a related-party transaction outside normal terms.
